title: Actionwitness
pitch: AI agents say “done.” ActionWitness proves it—checking WebMCP actions against real outcomes and turning failures into tamper-evident, replayable tests.
about_excerpt: AI agents say “done.” ActionWitness proves it—checking WebMCP actions against real outcomes and turning failures into tamper-evident, replayable tests. Like Comment Story Updates High level flow Storefront audit Agent webmcp tool call failure Agent webmcp tool call success landing page Regression Replay Inspiration Most WebMCP evaluation ask whether an agent called the right tool with valid arguments. That matters, but it stops at the tool's own response without evidence. Consider an agent calling apply_discount({code: "SAVE20"}) . The tool returns {"status": "success", "total": "20.00"} and the call-level evaluator passes it. But the shopper's cart still totals 25.00 . The call was well formed; the business outcome was wrong. This is a silent success . Nothing crashes, the logs look healthy, the agent moves on, and the user is given false confidence. I built ActionWitness to close that gap. The name is the thesis: The agent said it did the thing. ActionWitness shows what actually happened. ActionWitness complements call-level evaluators rather than replacing them. A call-level evaluator checks whether the model used the tool correctly. ActionWitness checks whether the tool produced the promised real-world outcome. Strong assurance needs both. What it does ActionWitness is a target-neutral assurance harness for WebMCP applications. It records what a tool claimed, independently observes authoritative business state, and evaluates both against a human-defined outcome contract. The core mechanism deliberately keeps two channels separate: Agent intent | +--> WebMCP tool call --------> tool-reported result (the claim) | +--> independent observer ----> authoritative business state (the outcome) | Human-defined contract ----------------------+--> deterministic verdict A successful tool response is evidence, never manufactured observed state. If the authoritative state is unavailable or the evidence chain cannot be verified, the result is an explicit non-pass—not a guessed success. ActionWitness provides: Outcome contracts. A human declares the required business outcome. A deterministic, target-neutral kernel produces the verdict; an LLM never acts as the authoritative judge. Independent observation. Tool output and observed state are stored as different evidence types with explicit source classification. Hash-linked evidence. Evidence is append-only, canonically serialized, content-addressed, and verified before it is trusted. Human confirmation. Consequential mutations require a server-issued confirmation bound to the workspace, run, action, arguments, and expiry. An agent cannot create, broaden, or approve its own consent. Fail-closed idempotency. Retries reuse a key only for identical intent. Reusing a key with changed intent is refused. Regression replay. A failed journey can produce a self-contained case that restores its fixture and reproduces the same classification locally or in CI. Repeated trials and correlation. Frozen intent variants run in isolated workspaces and correlate with imported Google webmcp-evals reports. Trials without a valid observation are excluded with a reason rather than counted as passes. Human-frozen intent variants. An optional Gemini backend drafts rephrasings, but generated rows arrive unapproved. Drafting and freezing use separate endpoints, so one call can never generate and approve an intent. The number a call-level evaluator cannot produce ActionWitness presents a simple disagreement matrix: Observed outcome passed Observed outcome failed Call-level evaluator passed Supported success Silent outcome failure Call-level evaluator failed Outcome succeeded despite call issue Both layers failed The key measure is straightforward: among the trials your call-level evaluator passed, how many still failed in observed business state? In our recorded demo suite, that silent outcome failure rate is 0.5000 . The UI names the disagreement cell in words rather than asking a reviewer to infer it from raw counts. Three proofs, not one A deterministic false-success target. The Buggy Store has pre_fix and post_fix modes. The same journey fails or passes with exactly one declared fault profile changed, making the evidence a controlled comparison rather than a staged assertion. An authorized Shopify development store. The integration is intentionally narrow: one operator-authorized development store, one server-controlled variant and currency, and cart-only behavior. Shopify's native WebMCP tools perform the agent-side actions. A reviewed theme bridge observes the shopper's own cart through Shopify's locale-aware, same-session /cart.js API—a channel independent of the tools' self-reports. The proof has been exercised end to end against the configured development store; checkout, orders, payments, bulk operations, and arbitrary remote targets remain out of scope. ActionWitness verifies itself. A separate self_target distribution drives ActionWitness through its public API and observes a different server-minted workspace through the same protocols used by third-party integrations. It declares only the target-neutral core and an HTTP client, so it cannot import the repository, service, or database. Pointing observation at the recording workspace instead makes the run fail with maximum_mutations : the product catches its own loss of observation independence. How I built it Python 3.12 owns contracts, orchestration, persistence, observation, evidence, evaluation, replay, and CLI behavior. FastAPI and Pydantic validate the service boundary. SQLite is the durable source of truth, evolved through ten explicit, tested migrations. React with strict TypeScript stays a minimal interaction and browser-integration layer; it does not duplicate Python-owned verdict or consent logic. All direct WebMCP access is isolated in frontend/src/webmcp/adapter.ts . The adapter resolves document.modelContext first and navigator.modelContext as a compatibility fallback, normalizes errors, propagates cancellation, and performs StrictMode-safe cleanup. The bundled harness and Buggy Store share one origin, while the authorized Shopify proof uses an explicitly configured external store and browser-session observer. ActionWitness publishes 17 lifecycle-scoped WebMCP tools , including seven read-only inspection tools for timelines, comparisons, regression cases, audit reports, and benchmark summaries. Only the tools valid for the current workspace phase are registered. The deliberate exclusions are just as important: an agent cannot approve consent, authorize an audit, submit its own audit evidence, freeze intent variants, or curate benchmark results. The repository's safety rules are executable gates rather than documentation alone. video_transcript_excerpt: WebMCP lets AI agents discover and use tools published by a web page, but when a tool returns success, that is still only a claim. It does not prove that the cart, record, or workflow actually changed. We built Action Witness to close this outcome gap with independent observation, human authorized intent, and replayable evidence. In this run, a browser agent discovers the page's WebMCP tools, searches the catalog, adds one mug, and applies save 20. The discount tool returns success. Action Witness records that result as reported evidence, but never converts it into truth. A separate observer reads the business state through a different channel. The observed cart total is wrong, so the verdict fails and names the mismatch. The WebMCP call looks successful, while reality did not. One click turns that failure into a content-addressed regression case, restores the original fixture, and replays the same classification locally or in CI. At evaluation scale, the model can draft variants, but a human freezes accepted intent into a content-hashed manifest. Drops arrive unticked, and generation can never approve them. Action Witness imports the call-level evaluator result and runs three bounded outcome trials with every row committed before execution. The matrix says the disagreement in plain language, evaluator passed, observed state failed. Every repetition exposes the same silent failure instead of averaging it away. Now the same proof model runs against a real Shopify development store. The browser invokes Shopify's native WebMCP update cart tool for one server-configured test variant. A small team bridge captures the cart before and after from the same shopper session. The authoritative read comes from Shopify's cart endpoint, not from the tool response. The update sets quantity two, yet this contract expected one, so the run correctly fails. Action Witness proves genuine success and convincing false success without admin access. Check out orders, customer login, or payment data. Action Witness can even verify itself. Its self-target adapter is structurally isolated from the repository and database using only public core contracts and HTTP. A separate observed workspace drives published tools to the public API point observation back at the recording workspace and Action Witness catches itself with a maximum mutations failure. Action Witness publishes seven read-only web MCP tools to inspect workspaces, runs, findings, evidence, correlation, and regressions. The exclusions matter. An agent cannot approve consent, authorize an audit, submit evidence, or curate benchmarks. Action Witness complements call evaluators with independent outcome proof. Verify what happened, preserve the evidence, replay what broke.
